story.what_it_does: IndiaMART runs an online B2B marketplace where buyers find suppliers, and suppliers pay subscriptions (such as Silver, Gold and Platinum tiers) to get enquiries. It also owns the BUSY business software unit. Management stresses it wants to stay a software company rather than move to a transaction-based model.
story.plans: Management aims for double-digit growth in the near term and a long-run EBITDA margin of about 33%. It targets 27-30% BUSY growth over the next couple of years and plans bank account verification of free customers (50% next year, 80% in two years). It says it will not invest in gross supplier additions until churn improves.
story.moat: The company has a large network of about 217 thousand paying suppliers, 8.9 million storefronts and 42 million active buyers, plus Rs 3,234 crore of cash and investments. Its margins are high (consolidated 37%, standalone 40%). However, the notes show enquiries falling as Google AI Overviews and LLMs divert traffic, which tests how durable the network is.

scenarios.story: Price-led realization keeps lifting revenue while verification of free customers cuts churn and stabilizes the supplier base. BUSY grows at the targeted 27-30% and margins stay above the 33% long-term guide.
signals_to_watch: Paying supplier count returning to net additions after the declines of 1,200, 1,850 and 615
BUSY revenue growth staying near the 27-30% target

scenarios.story: Revenue grows around 10% a year, driven by better realization from each paying supplier rather than more suppliers. Margins stay healthy but enquiry trends stay volatile over the next couple of years, as management says.
